title: The First Monday
focus: 听懂入职安排，并主动确认自己的任务
story:
My new work card does not open the door. I hold it against the black square again. A red light appears, followed by a short, unfriendly sound.

“Turn it over,” says someone behind me.

Rui stands there with two paper cups. I turn the card over. This time the light is green.

“Excellent technical work,” he says, giving me one cup.

I laugh, although I have spent the whole train journey trying to look like a person who belongs here.

Northstar occupies one floor of an office building near a busy Shanghai road. From the lift, I can hear drills somewhere below us. Inside, the office smells of coffee and new carpet. Rui shows me an empty desk with a monitor, a keyboard and a little packet of screws.

“The monitor stand needs one of those,” he says. “Don't throw them away.”

Three weeks have passed since the offer. I have read the documents twice, bought a notebook and checked the route. None of that tells me what to do with my coat.

Daniel arrives while I am putting it over my chair. He carries a laptop under one arm.

“Welcome, Andy. Sorry, it's a busy morning. Have you got access?”

“To the office, yes.”

He smiles briefly. “I mean the development system.”

“Not yet.”

“IT will help. Read the project notes, then sit with Rui. There's a client call later. Just listen today.”

He is already looking towards a meeting room.

“What time is the call?” I ask.

“Four thirty. I'll send the invitation.”

His answer is perfectly ordinary. I feel foolish for needing courage to ask the question.

By lunch, I can open the code and the team messages. I cannot run the application. A small error box covers the screen. Rui leans across the space between our desks.

“Did you install the local database?”

“I followed the setup page.”

He reads it and makes a noise through his teeth. “Old instructions. Wait.”

I nearly apologise. Then I stop. The page is old; my English has not broken the database.

We find the missing step together. I add it to the page while Rui checks that the application starts. A calendar appears, full of imaginary classes: drawing, basic computing, English conversation.

“The client runs community learning centres,” Rui explains. “They need one place for bookings and schedules.”

He opens a class with twelve enrolled learners.

“This part is ours. Staff change a class time, and the system tells the learners.”

“That sounds simple.”

Rui looks at me. “It sounds simple.”

“Can I stay beside you this afternoon?” I ask. “Just until the call?”

Rui looks at his calendar. “Until two. I promised someone I'd look at their work after that.”

“I'll sit quietly.”

“You say that now.” He turns his screen towards me. There are already three little windows with his name in them. “I like having you here, Andy. I also liked having lunch.”

I notice the unopened sandwich under his monitor. It is almost two already. I take my notebook back to my own desk.

For a while I keep a list of everything I want to ask him. Then I try a class change on my own. The calendar has two classes called Drawing. The first is full; the second has only four names. I had assumed I was seeing the same class twice. When I look at the details, one meets on Tuesday, the other on Thursday. I cross out my first question. My second is better: if staff move Tuesday's class to Thursday, how will the people reading the message know which class has moved?

I leave that one on the page. Across the aisle Rui finally opens his sandwich. He has cut it in half. Someone comes over carrying a laptop before he can pick up the second half.

At four thirty, we sit in a small room. Elena joins from London. Behind her, a woman walks past carrying a pile of folders. Elena asks us to wait while she finds her headphones.

Daniel introduces me. I have prepared two sentences, but my name comes out too quietly. Elena moves closer to her camera.

“Sorry, could you say that again?”

“I'm Andy. I'll be working on the booking system with Rui.”

“Welcome. I hope he hasn't shown you all our complicated spreadsheets yet.”

“Only the calendar.”

“Then there's still hope.”

Everyone laughs. I do too, a second late.

During the call, I understand the main problem. Centre staff currently copy changes between several lists. But I lose a discussion about which list is the official record. I write a question mark beside it instead of pretending I understand.

After the call, Daniel points at my notebook.

“All clear?”

My mouth starts to form yes.

“Mostly. Which list should we use if two records disagree?”

He puts his laptop down again. “Good question. We haven't agreed that yet. Don't build a rule for it.”

I underline those last words.

At home, Maya is cutting a large sheet of blue paper on the table. Small triangles cover the floor.

“How was Monday?” she asks.

“I fixed some instructions. Asked two questions. Failed to open a door.”

“Busy day.”

She moves her cutting mat towards her side. “I have a presentation tomorrow. Can I keep this half until ten?”

“Of course. I'll eat here.” I point to the clear corner.

While my rice warms, I open my notebook. Under tomorrow's date, I write the question I did not ask: what should I finish this week?

Maya reaches across the table for a piece of tape. “What's the question?”

I read it to her.

“And who's got the answer?”

“Daniel.”

“Good. For a moment I thought it was me.”

She sticks a paper sign to the back of a chair and walks to the hallway to look at it. I carry my bowl around her line of sight. In the morning, before I even take my coat off, I stop at Daniel's desk and ask him. He wants me to take the little window that confirms a class change. I can see the whole thing in my head. Two buttons and a time. I tell him I'd like to do it.

phrases.en: What should I finish this week?

practice.grammar: 现在完成时用于说明截至目前的状态：I haven’t got access yet. 用 yet 区分“还没有”和“永远不会”。再说一个你尚未完成的准备事项。
practice.pronunciation: 按意群说：I’m Andy / and I’ll be working / on the booking system. 每个斜线处短停，重读 Andy、working、booking，重复三遍后不看文字再说。

questions.q: Why can Andy not run the application at first?
questions.a: The setup page is missing a step about the local database.

questions.q: Why does Rui ask Andy to work at his own desk after two?
questions.a: Rui has already promised to review someone else's work.

questions.q: Why does Maya need half the table?
questions.a: She is preparing materials for a presentation the next day.

roleplay.context: 你是第一天入职的 Andy。先说明访问问题，再确认工作范围。

turns.line: Have you got everything you need?
turns.cue: 说明办公室门卡可用，但开发系统权限还没有。

turns.line: Just read the notes for now.

turns.cue: 说明两份记录冲突，需要确认依据。

practice.transfer: 你第一次参加社区课程。用英语向接待员确认教室、开始时间，以及需要提前准备的东西；至少问三个具体问题。
practice.retell: 用一至两分钟复述第一天的三个小困难。每次先说问题，再说 Andy 做了什么；最后说出他留下的一个问题。
